taskPacket.objective: Every judge canary case says who wrote it, and the canary report gives recall and false alarms per author family as well as in total (R1).
instructions: Add authoredBy to every task packet and every defect in evals/judge-canary/corpus.json. authoredBy is an object {runtime, family}: runtime is the runtime id that wrote the text (for example claude-opus-5-5), family is its vendor family, one of anthropic, openai, deepseek, zhipu, google (the vocabulary of evals/judge-canary/runtimes.json's vendor field). Every one of the 10 tasks and 25 defects today was written by the node canary-rebuilt of evals-with-a-budget (worker claude-opus-5-5, no failover; measured 2026-09-24 from its usage ledger and git history), so each gets {"runtime": "claude-opus-5-5", "family": "anthropic"}.

The builder (evals/judge-canary.mjs) refuses a task or defect without a valid authoredBy, and carries it into each built case (case.json): a defect case carries its defect's authoredBy, a clean control carries its task's (the packet's author). Bump BUILDER_VERSION, since the case format changes, and rebuild the committed cases with `node evals/judge-canary.mjs` (about two minutes).
authoredBy must never reach the judge: not in the prompt, not in any file of the workspace a harness judge reviews. Extend the existing leak test so it also covers authoredBy.

evals/judge-canary/class.mjs: each outcome carries the case's author family, and the report gains byAuthorFamily: for each family, the defect verdicts, rejected, cited rejections and recall (computed exactly as the per-label recall is), and the clean verdicts and false-alarm rate. Errored verdicts stay outside both rates, as they are today. The rendered report shows it. Provenance's runtimes entries also carry the judge's vendor, read from evals/judge-canary/runtimes.json.

Pin two tests in test/evals/judge-canary.test.mjs: 'the canary reports recall by the family that authored each defect' (a fake judge over cases from two author families gives different recall per family and the right totals), and 'the committed canary cases are what the corpus builds' (the case ids, each diffSha256 and each authoredBy on disk equal what buildCanaryArtifacts produces from corpus.json; it must not run the verifications).

taskPacket.objective: One command turns the versioned judge canary results into a matrix: for each worker vendor family, the judges the vendor rule allows, with their numbers, and the best one marked (R3).
instructions: New module evals/judge-canary-matrix.mjs, runnable as `node evals/judge-canary-matrix.mjs [--result-dir <dir>] <result.json>...`. It reads judge-canary result files (the shape evals/judge-canary/class.mjs writes), pools each judge runtime's outcomes over every file and repetition given for it, and never invokes a model.
It refuses (exit 2, naming the file) a result that is not class judge-canary, that has no provenance.corpusHash, or whose corpusHash differs from the others: judges are only comparable on one corpus.

Per judge runtime: id, vendor (provenance runtimes' vendor, added by the canary-authorship node; a result without it is refused), result files, repetitions, cases, recall, false-alarm rate, errors, cost per case in USD, and recall and false-alarm rate per author family (byAuthorFamily). Compute pooled rates from the pooled counts, not by averaging per-file rates.

Worker families: anthropic, deepseek, google, openai, zhipu, the five vendors the product's harnesses talk to (see the header of src/engine/pricing-seed.mjs; zhipuai there is zhipu here). For each family, the allowed judges are the measured judges whose vendor differs from that family (the rule in src/contract/index.mjs near line 293). The best allowed judge: take the highest recall among the allowed; among the allowed judges whose recall is at least that minus 0.05, pick the lowest cost per case; break a remaining tie by the lower false-alarm rate, then by id. A family with no allowed judge says so.

Output: a JSON file matrix-<timestamp>.json in --result-dir (default evals/results/judge-canary/) with the inputs (paths and corpusHash), the per-judge table and the per-family rows, and a markdown table on stdout (one row per worker family, one column per allowed judge showing recall / false alarm / USD per case, the best marked). Document the command in evals/README.md in a short paragraph.

Pin the test 'the canary report says which judges may judge each worker vendor' in the new file test/evals/judge-canary-matrix.test.mjs, over fixture result objects written to a temp directory: it checks the allowed sets, the best-judge rule including the 0.05 cost window, pooling across two files of one judge, and the refusal of mixed corpus hashes.

taskPacket.objective: Five judge canary defects, one per kind, are written by gpt-6-sol and replace five written by claude-opus-5-5 (R2, first half).
instructions: You write five new defect cases for the judge canary, one per kind, and each replaces one existing defect written by claude-opus-5-5. You are the author: every new entry carries authoredBy {"runtime": "gpt-6-sol", "family": "openai"}. The point of the work is that these defects come from a model family other than the one that wrote the rest of the corpus, so write each one yourself from the task's golden diff and packet. Do not copy, paraphrase or vary an existing defect's edits, and do not ask for or reuse text from any other source.

Remove exactly these defect entries from evals/judge-canary/corpus.json (by task and kind): nongoal-violated on deny-the-out-of-scope-write-before-the-file-exists; requirement-half-done on report-the-provider-s-startup-error-not-just-an-empty-stream; scope-drift-inside-writefiles on classify-codex-tool-host-failure-before-cancellation; doc-contradicts-code on deny-the-out-of-scope-write-before-the-file-exists; test-weakened on deny-the-out-of-scope-write-before-the-file-exists.

Add exactly these defect entries (by kind and task), each with kind, task, description, edits and authoredBy: nongoal-violated on anthropic-soft-limit-fixture; requirement-half-done on stop-re-sealing-a-clean-attempt-from-failing-the-retry; scope-drift-inside-writefiles on strip-the-notification-transport-from-worker-provider-enviro; doc-contradicts-code on deepseek-balance-classification; test-weakened on carry-git-s-own-reason-into-a-failed-git-command.

The five kinds, as evals/README.md and the existing corpus use them: nongoal-violated (the diff does something the packet's non-goals exclude), requirement-half-done (a behaviour the packet requires is only partly implemented while the result claims it done), scope-drift-inside-writefiles (an unrequested change inside the files the task may write), doc-contradicts-code (a comment or document the diff adds or edits states something the code does not do), test-weakened (a test the diff adds or edits no longer asserts what its name and the instructions claim).

How a defect is built: evals/judge-canary.mjs applies each defect's edits (find/replace line arrays) to the task's golden diff, only inside files the golden diff already changes. Read the golden task under evals/golden/<task>/ (statement.md, meta.json, verify.json) and its golden diff with `git diff <parentSha> <commitSha>` from meta.json. The packet the judge sees is the task's entry in corpus.json. A good defect is one a careful reviewer finds by reading the diff against the packet, and that the task's own verification does not catch.

Rebuild with `node evals/judge-canary.mjs` (about two minutes). The builder refuses, by case id, a defect the task's verification catches, and a corpus with fewer than five defects per kind over distinct tasks; when it refuses one of yours, change that defect until it passes. Commit nothing yourself; leave the rebuilt case directories and manifest.json in the worktree.
Do not edit any other defect, any task packet or any clean control. The description of each new defect states the defect plainly (it never reaches the judge).
